description: Well oiled machine hailing all the way from Emeris Pretoria
summary: Astracare is an offline-first astronaut health-monitoring application developed to help crew members manage health concerns during space missions. The app allows users to record vital signs and symptoms, identify unusual readings, and receive alerts connected to relevant medical guidance and emergency procedures. It addresses the challenge of delayed communication with Earth by providing immediate, locally stored health support without requiring an internet connection. Astracare is important because it can help astronauts recognize potential health problems earlier, respond appropriately, and maintain access to essential information in isolated environments.
details: Astracare was developed using C++17, Qt 6, CMake, SQLite, and JSON files. The application checks health data against configurable reference ranges and displays normal, cautionary, or urgent alerts. It also supports role-based access to sensitive clinical information. The project is creative because it combines astronaut health tracking, emergency guidance, trend detection, and a space-themed interface in one system. Our team considered privacy, usability during stressful situations, offline functionality, communication delays, data accuracy, security, and the need for medical professionals to review the guidance before real-world use.
